message.content: {"6374_8353801528149": {"answer": "B", "reason": "The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 1) shows a large, well-circumscribed opacity in the posterior right hemithorax that forms an obtuse angle with the chest wall, a classic sign of an extrapulmonary (pleural or chest wall) origin."}, "6374_8353801540437": {"answer": "B", "reason": "The imaging demonstrates a homogeneous, well-defined mass with an obtuse angle to the chest wall, which is characteristic of an extrapulmonary lesion such as a pleural mass rather than a pulmonary nodule."}, "6374_8353801543173": {"answer": "D", "reason": "Malignant mesothelioma typically presents as a pleural-based mass with an obtuse angle to the chest wall, often accompanied by calcifications (from prior asbestos exposure) and pleural nodules."}, "6374_8353801548945": {"answer": "D", "reason": "The presence of a mass with nodularity and involvement of the mediastinal pleura (as seen in Figure 3) is highly characteristic of malignant mesothelioma, distinguishing it from benign pleural disease or simple effusions."}, "6374_8353801549317": {"answer": "F", "reason": "The mass is located posteriorly in the right hemithorax (confirmed by lateral view and CT), and while associated with a small effusion, the absence of extensive diffuse thickening or nodularity on the plain film represents a less typical or localized presentation of mesothelioma."}}
